Toyota Connected (EU)

Making Smart Charging
effortless

2024

01 Context 02 User Research 03 Challenges 04 Looking to Competitors 05 Solutions 06 Outcomes
01 Context

Setting the Scene

My Role

When I joined the European Toyota App team, Toyota was investing heavily in EV technology and launching a new energy management area within the app, designed to help users understand, control, and optimise energy between their car and home.

As Lead Product Designer, I owned the end-to-end experience, from discovery and research through to flow design, stakeholder alignment, and testing.

Team Setup

The work was happening within an established team structure and delivery culture that really pushed for "just implement it." My role became not just about redesigning the experience, but also introducing stronger design thinking and more realistic delivery talks, often directly with senior stakeholders at Toyota.

Business Objectives
  • Optimise vehicle charging costs with a seamless EV charging experience
  • Educate users about the benefits and capabilities of V1G technology
  • Develop user-friendly interfaces for Smart Charging controls that accommodate varying energy needs and preferences
02 User Research

Understanding Users

The feature needs to work for current Toyota EV owners already using Smart Charging, new EV owners just learning about the concept, and future users of upcoming technologies like Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G).

To understand expectations, behaviours, and mental models, I worked with a UX research specialist to interview both EV owners and non-EV owners, supported by a detailed questionnaire.

Findings
  1. Users primarily cared about how much charge their vehicle has
  2. Cost of charging was the second priority
  3. Users expected to access and manage this information easily from their smartphone
03 Challenges

Uncovering Ownership Gaps

In parallel, I also surveyed internal stakeholders to understand how the feature had evolved, who owned which parts of the experience, and where handoffs were breaking down. It became clear that multiple teams owning different components had resulted in a loss of journey fluency for the user.

Fragmented Experience and Discoverability

A full evaluation of the current experience revealed that Smart Charging was deeply buried in settings, with little signposting or explanation. Users had no way to understand the value proposition before committing to the setup flow and why they would benefit from using it.

But the biggest issue users were facing — just when simply trying to turn on the feature using the switch — was multiple pop-up windows appearing based on their current settings. This was due to technical constraints that needed to be addressed before scheduling could be turned on, but it presented a disjointed and annoying experience for the user.

04 Looking to Competitors

Learning from Competitors

I reviewed competitor apps to understand how Smart Charging was explained and framed, how setup journeys were structured and which features were considered baseline expectations. I then mapped these into a feature comparison, identifying must-haves, nice-to-haves, and gaps in Toyota's current offering.

Some clear themes emerged that showed which features were essential:

  • A guided setup flow
  • An override option to charge immediately
  • Charging statistics, usually visualised in graphs
  • Visibility of upcoming scheduled charges

Most of these were missing or poorly implemented.

05 Solutions

Fixing the Core Problem

Rather than layering improvements on top of a broken experience, the focus shifted to fixing the fundamentals.

The feature needed to be visible, signposted more clearly in the app for EV users, with benefits explained using language that reflected the top user priorities mentioned above: charge level, cost, and control. Most importantly, the feature setup needed to feel simple and linear. I designed a new guided setup flow that walked users step by step through the process.

06 Outcomes

Testing and Early Outcomes

The redesigned journey was prepared for launch in the UK and Sweden, where Toyota was partnering with local energy and services providers. User testing focused primarily on UK users and the participants were guided through the new setup experience and prompted to let us know things like missing information, any points of confusion, and any moments of reassurance or uncertainty.

Results were documented in detail and presented back to stakeholders, helping align product, engineering, and leadership around why the changes mattered, not just what had changed.

Impact and Next Steps

While this work was completed ahead of launch and did not yet have live performance data, user testing showed a significant improvement in understanding and confidence when setting up Smart Charging.

The redesigned journey also helped align product, engineering, and leadership around a shared vision for energy management.

Beyond Smart Charging — Broadening the Scope

Smart Charging (V1G) is just one part of a much bigger energy management piece. Looking ahead, some Toyota vehicles in the next decade will have Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) capabilities, allowing users to not only charge their cars, but also send energy back to the grid and get paid for it. This added a whole new level of complexity for us.

To explore this future state, I worked closely with a Service Designer to define a long-term vision for Toyota's energy management experience. Together, we mapped out how this could all come together into a single, coherent narrative.
